title: Phase 10: Platform extras
description:
Capability: the platform talks back. The Overview feed gets filters and a cross-project view, Slack notifications fire
on bot finish, incidents and deploys, and a native platform chat agent (Digital Hub's Hub agent, as the first Mastra
agent) can navigate the app. Jack adds the LLM gateway key and model when he reaches this phase; until then the agent is
declared but hidden. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-10-platform-extras.md.
Human test: filter the Overview feed to incidents; turn on "notify when a bot finishes" and receive the Slack message
with a thread link; add the gateway key, define the model, ask the agent to open uptime for a project and to start a
chat with Claude Code.

title: Phase 9: Operations: deployments (firm parts)
description:
Capability: per project, see what is live per environment, and (later) deploy a branch through the project's vendor.
This phase is deliberately open; only the firm parts are decomposed here: the Netlify and Heroku plugin types, the
common live-version shape with vendor and custom-endpoint sources, and the Deployments page showing them. The deploy
zone (per-environment deploy strategies for Netlify build hooks, Heroku pushes, GitHub Actions dispatch, Bitbucket
pipelines, and record-only) is NOT decomposed; Jack will refine it when he reaches it, and it must write a
`deploy.attempted` activity event per attempt. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-9-operations-deployments.md.
Human test: Netlify configured shows the current deploy's commit and branch; a second environment from the project's own
version endpoint renders the same fields.

title: Phase 8: Operations: uptime
description:
Capability: per project, register things to ping, see their state and history, and get incidents when they go down.
Monitors are rows, not a JSON file; the poller survives restarts without duplicates; state uses Digital Hub's
hysteresis so blips do not flap. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-8-operations-uptime.md. Research:
.ai-docs/research/digital-hub.md section 6.
Human test: an HTTP monitor against a toggleable fake service and a Statuspage monitor go green; toggling off goes
degraded then down with an incident on the Overview feed; toggling on closes it; a restart keeps history, rebuilds state
without a false incident and runs one poller per monitor; editing an interval changes cadence without a restart.

title: Phase 7: Slack surface
description:
Capability: team members mention a bot in Slack and it works the request in its worktree, streams progress into the
thread, asks for decisions with buttons, and ends with a structured handoff card. Socket Mode, outbound only, keys from
the secrets store, so it works with no public URL. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-7-slack-surface.md.
Research: .ai-docs/research/clanker-corner.md section 7.
Human test: keys added shows connected; a roster mention in a listed channel streams progress, a permission answered
by button disappears from the chat panel, the handoff card shows summary, PR link and issue id; a reply continues the
session; a daemon restart mid-turn recovers with one completion; non-listed channel and non-member get silence; the bot
posts Block Kit through the MCP tool.

title: Phase 6: Bots and team, with worktree isolation
description:
Capability: define a bot for a project, point it at a persona in the repo, choose its agent and write scope, list who
may talk to it, and run it in an isolated git worktree from the chat panel before Slack is connected. Lifts Clanker
Corner's worktree pool, posture model and persona checks; bots never touch the project's main checkout.
Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-6-bots-and-team.md. Research: .ai-docs/research/clanker-corner.md
sections 2, 3, 5, 6.
Human test: persona check disables Codex when only the Claude persona exists; a console thread with the bot creates a
worktree on a new branch, edits prompt for confirmation, `bd close` from the bot shows on the Issues page, the main
checkout is untouched, a push asks first, and the worktree is reclaimed only after the work is pushed.

title: Phase 5: Run issues with an agent
description:
Capability: from an issue, or a selection of issues, start a Claude Code or Codex chat that works on them, and create
issues by interviewing an agent. The platform does not orchestrate: the prompt is fixed and the codebase's own skills
decide how the agent works. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-5-run-issues.md.
Human test: Run from an issue opens a thread with the exact prompt; Run from the bulk bar lists all ids; without the
Repository plugin Run is disabled with the reason; Create with Claude Code produces an issue that appears live; both runs
show on the Overview feed.

title: Phase 4: Agent sessions and chat panel
description:
Capability: Claude Code and Codex are configured per project (each plugin owns a private config home and a CLI login),
and Jack can chat with either from a panel on any page, with permission prompts answered in the UI and transcripts that
survive reloads and daemon restarts. ACP is spoken through the ACP SDK directly (never Mastra's wrapper, which drops
events and needed patches); Clanker Corner's Claude shim is lifted as a workspace package.
Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-4-agent-sessions-and-chat.md. Research: .ai-docs/research/clanker-corner.md
sections 3 and 4, .ai-docs/research/candy-mountain-v2.md section 4.
Human test: log Claude Code in through the plugin page, Codex with the device flow, enable Agent Hub, chat with each,
see tool calls stream, deny then allow a permission, reload mid-turn with the transcript intact, restart the daemon and
continue the thread.

title: Add the Add Issue chooser and the write-it-yourself form
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. several). Done creates the issue through the daemon and navigates to its page.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria:
Creating an issue with a parent and two dependencies from the form is confirmed by `bd show` showing both; the
page navigates to the new issue; the agent options are absent on a project with no agent plugin.

acceptance_criteria:

within the cache window run `bd` once (test with a spy); a project without `.beads` yields a clear error.

description:

boundaries keep layers honest, and v3 wants the rules in place before any layer exists so later work only adds

title: Add SQLite through Drizzle with migrations and a configurable data directory
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. scattered state across JSON files; this hurt every time a schema changed. The daemon must own exactly one SQLite
database managed through Drizzle, with migrations generated from the schema and applied automatically on daemon
start. Introduce a single configurable data directory (environment variable with a sensible default under the
user's home, never inside any repository) that holds the database and, for later work, secrets, worktrees, agent
config homes and logs; moving to another machine must be a copy of that directory. Create the directory tree on
start. Provide a small, reusable way for later features to get the database handle and the data-directory paths.
Non-goals: no application tables beyond what proves the migration path works.
acceptance_criteria:
Starting the daemon on an empty data directory creates it and the database with migrations applied; a second
start is a no-op; a new migration added to the schema is applied on the next start; the data directory location
is configurable and documented; a test covers migration-on-start.

title: Build the encrypted write-only secrets store
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Plugins, bots and auth will hold tokens and keys that must never leave the daemon in plaintext and must survive a
move to another machine. Build a secrets store modelled on Candy Mountain v2's: values encrypted with AES-256-GCM
under a master key supplied by the operator (environment variable, 32 bytes, documented), written atomically with
restrictive file permissions or into the platform database as ciphertext (implementer's choice), and keyed by an
owner (for example a plugin instance or a bot) plus a secret name. The API is write-only: callers can set, check
whether a value is set, delete, and obtain the decrypted value only through an internal daemon-side accessor that
is never reachable from an HTTP route. Deleting an owner must delete all of its secrets. Redact secret values from
errors and logs. Non-goals: no OAuth, no rotation, no UI.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit tests prove set/is-set/delete/get-internal behaviour, that a wrong master key fails to decrypt, that deleting
an owner removes its secrets, and that no exported HTTP-facing function returns a secret value; the store lives
under the daemon's data directory.

title: Add the global Slack plugin type for platform notifications
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Notifications need a Slack identity when a project has no bot. Add the `slack` plugin type: global scope only
(the one global plugin in v3), secret is a bot token, config is a default channel id. Health means the token can
call Slack's auth test. Expose a daemon-side operation to post a message (text or blocks) to a channel or as a
direct message to a member id.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria:
A platform-level instance with a valid token reports healthy; the post operation delivers a message; a project
scope is rejected; tests mock Slack.

title: Schedule monitors on their own intervals with one poller per monitor
description:

Checks must keep running across restarts without ever running twice. Build the scheduler: on daemon start, load
every enabled monitor and schedule it on its interval (staggered so they do not all fire at once); creating,
editing (interval or target) or disabling a monitor reschedules it without a restart; deleting stops it. Each
check runs the type's checker and stores a check row (monitor, time, ok, status, latency, error), keeping a bounded

title: Derive monitor state with hysteresis and open and close incidents
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A single blip must not flap a monitor. Derive each monitor's state from its recent checks the way Digital Hub does:
down when the newest three checks all failed; degraded when any check in the recent window failed or latency
exceeded two seconds; up otherwise; unknown with no history. Rebuild state from stored history on start so a
restart never produces a false transition. Open an incident (monitor, opened at, reason) on the transition to
down and close it (closed at) on recovery to up; both write activity events (`incident.opened`,
`incident.closed`) linking to the monitor. Leave an optional thread-reference field on the incident for a later
investigation thread; nothing investigates automatically. Expose state, recent checks and incidents (per monitor
and project-wide) over REST.

Shared names: Activity event types are fixed strings: `session.started`, `run.started`, `bot.handoff`, `incident.opened`, `incident.closed`, `deploy.attempted`.
acceptance_criteria:
Three consecutive failures open one incident; recovery closes it; a single failure shows degraded without an
incident; restarting with a down monitor keeps the open incident and opens no second one; the Overview feed shows
both events; tests cover the transitions.

title: Implement the check runners for HTTP and the vendor status-page types

acceptance_criteria:
Unit tests with mocked HTTP cover ok, wrong status, missing substring, timeout and each vendor's degraded response;
a real check against a local fake service works.

title: Expose a thread-scoped MCP tool that lets the bot post Block Kit
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. This is the pattern for every "wrapped MCP server scoped to an agent" in Candy Mountain: the agent sees a narrow
tool while the daemon holds the credentials and the scope. Build a small MCP server the daemon runs for a bot
session (stdio or local HTTP, implementer's choice) exposing one tool that posts a Block Kit payload to the
current Slack thread. The daemon validates the payload (well-formed blocks, size limits, no raw tokens), posts it
with the bot's credentials, and refuses anything outside the current thread. Register the server with the agent
at session start through the harness (Claude Code and Codex both accept MCP server configuration), and allow the
tool in the posture for every write scope. Non-goals: any other tool.
acceptance_criteria:
Asking the bot to post a formatted message results in a Block Kit message in the thread; a payload naming another
channel is refused; the tool is absent from a plain console session that is not a bot.

title: Parse the structured handoff block from a final message
description:

Every Slack bot is asked to end a turn with a fenced handoff block, and the platform renders it rather than
trusting the model to write Block Kit. Write a pure parser: given the final assistant message, find the handoff
block, parse its fields, validate the outcome value, normalise "none" to empty, and return either the parsed
handoff or a reason it was missing or malformed. Tolerate surrounding prose and minor whitespace differences.

Shared names: The structured handoff format is fixed: a fenced code block whose info string is `handoff`, containing one `key: value` line per field with keys `outcome` (one of done, partial, blocked), `summary` (one line), `pull_request` (URL or none), `issues` (comma-separated issue ids or none), and `follow_ups` (semicolon-separated or none).
acceptance_criteria:

missing optional fields.

title: Route Slack mentions and replies to bot sessions with membership, resume and dedup
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A mention starts work; replies continue it. Build the router: a top-level mention of a bot, in a channel it
answers in (anywhere, or one of its listed channel ids), by a roster member whose scope covers the bot, creates a
thread-to-session mapping (bot, channel, thread timestamp, session, member) and starts a bot session with the
Slack thread as holder, passing the request text wrapped as context on the first turn (who asked, where, and the
message). Replies in a mapped thread continue the session; after a daemon restart the first reply resumes it.
Non-members and non-listed channels get silence. A thread whose member was removed from the roster stops being
answered. The word "done" alone in the thread closes the session and releases the worktree. Record every delivered
Slack event id so a retried event is never processed twice. Post the agent's final text to the thread (replaced
by streaming in separate work). Add an acknowledging reaction on receipt.
acceptance_criteria:
A roster mention in a listed channel starts a session and a worktree; a reply continues it; a mention from a
non-member or non-listed channel gets no reply; a replayed event is ignored; after restart a reply resumes the
same session; "done" releases the worktree; tests cover gating and dedup.

title: Stream progress into the Slack thread with exactly-once completion

A turn shows live text and tool summaries in the thread; restarting the daemon mid-turn ends with exactly one
completed message; the fallback path works when native streaming is unavailable; tests cover the persistence.

title: Manage one Socket Mode connection per active bot

Slack bot token and app-level token are set, open a Socket Mode connection using those secrets, reconnect with
backoff on failure, and track connection state (connecting, connected, disconnected with reason) exposed on the

implements; acknowledge events promptly. Also expose a Slack Web API client per bot for posting.

keys closes the connection; a dropped network reconnects; tests mock the Slack client.

title: Run a bot session end to end: worktree, persona, posture, instructions, decisions
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

This is the real bot path, used by the console and later by Slack. Build the bot session starter in the daemon:
given a bot and a holder (console thread or Slack thread), run the persona check, acquire or resume the worktree
lease for the holder, compute the posture for the bot's family and scope, compose the surface instructions, apply
the environment that routes `bd` to the main checkout's database, and start or resume a session through the
existing session layer with the worktree as working directory and the project's plugin config home. Decisions
flow through the existing pending-decision model. Closing the holder releases the lease under the safe-reclaim
rule. Record failures (persona missing, worktree cap, plugin unhealthy) as typed reasons the caller can show.

title: Map write scope to agent posture per family and verify it is never widened
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Write scope is the human's promise about what a bot may do, and nothing may widen it. Build the posture mapping
for a bot session: for Claude Code, read-only becomes plan mode with the tools that leave plan mode or spawn agents
denied; write-with-confirmation becomes the default permission mode; write-automatically becomes accept-edits with
the shell sandbox on and git push always asking. All scopes: disable every hook from the checkout, pass the persona
as the CLI's agent, always allow the `bd` command, and vet the checkout's own Claude settings files so they cannot
auto-approve shell commands. For Codex, map the same scopes onto its approval and sandbox settings (read-only
sandbox for read-only; workspace-write with on-request approvals for both write scopes) and pass the persona as
developer instructions. Refuse any resulting configuration that bypasses permissions, and refuse a persona whose
front matter asks for broader permissions than the scope allows. The output is the launch flags, environment and
config the harness passes through.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit tests assert the flags and config for every scope and family; a persona front matter requesting bypass is
refused; a checkout settings file that auto-approves shell commands is neutralised; `bd` is always allowed.

title: Make bd inside a worktree read and write the project's main beads database
description:

created inside the worktree; the helper is documented.

title: Build the worktree pool with persisted leases and caps
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Bots must never work in the checkout Jack edits. Build a worktree pool in the daemon: the project's local path is
the clone, and a bot session gets its own git worktree under the daemon's data directory on its own branch
(named to identify the bot and session) cut from a given base branch after fetching it. Leases are rows in the
platform database (project, holder kind and id, path, branch, base branch, state, timestamps) so a resumed session
lands in the same path, which both CLIs need to find their conversation. Refuse to create a worktree on the base
branch itself. Enforce a configurable cap on concurrent worktrees per project. Serialise all git operations on a
clone with a per-project lock so concurrent sessions do not corrupt it. Provide acquire, resume (by holder), and
release operations. Non-goals: reclaim policy and dependency installation (separate work).

title: Reclaim idle worktrees safely and reconcile orphans at startup
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Worktrees accumulate; reclaiming one must never lose work. Add a reclaim pass to the worktree pool: a lease whose
holder has been idle for a configurable period is reclaimed only if its worktree has no uncommitted changes and no
commits that are not on the remote; otherwise it is kept and marked as holding unpushed work so the UI can show
it. Releasing a lease explicitly follows the same safety rule. On daemon startup reconcile: leases whose paths are
missing are closed, worktrees on disk with no lease are removed if clean and reported if not, and git's own
worktree list is pruned.
acceptance_criteria:
An idle clean worktree is reclaimed; one with an uncommitted file is kept and flagged; one with an unpushed commit
is kept; after deleting a worktree directory by hand, startup closes its lease; tests cover each case.

v2 lost every transcript on reload or restart, which is why its harness chat felt unfinished. Add a session model
in the daemon: a session belongs to a project, an agent family, an actor and a working directory, and records its
upstream ACP session id so it can be resumed after a daemon restart. Every event the harness emits for a session
is appended to a durable per-session event log in the platform database with a sequence number. Expose per-session
REST: send a prompt (starting or resuming the live process on demand), cancel, and a server-sent event stream

title: Model permission requests and agent questions as pending decisions
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Agents ask for permission and sometimes ask questions; the human must answer, and never by accident. Add a
pending-decision model on top of sessions: each harness permission request or elicitation becomes a decision
record (session, kind, the options the agent offered with their kinds, a timeout) that is logged as an event, and
an endpoint answers it. Rules learned from v2 and Clanker: a decision is answered by option kind (allow once,
always allow, deny, or a typed answer), never by position; "always allow" may only accept rules the agent itself
proposed; an answer for an unknown or already-answered decision is rejected; an unanswered decision times out to
refusal after a configurable period; anything unexpected is refused. Design the model so another surface (Slack,
later) can answer the same decision, and the first answer wins. Add a never-bypass rule: no configuration path
may launch either agent in a bypass-permissions mode; refuse such settings by name.
acceptance_criteria:
A permission request appears as a pending decision on the stream; answering deny stops the tool; answering allow
continues it; a second answer is rejected; a timed-out decision is refused; a launch configuration containing a
bypass mode is refused; tests cover each.
